parsed.explanation: The induction claims to characterize all finite transversals whenever C is merely a finite transversal. But its argument only treats transversals X with X∩C≠∅. At recursive calls, C\{c} need not belong to F_c, so there is no reason every transversal of F_c must meet it. The witness F={{1,2},{2,3}}, C={2}, X={1,3} satisfies all stated hypotheses: F is pairwise intersecting, C is a transversal, and X is a transversal disjoint from C. Thus the proposed criterion misses X. Since the top-level proof invokes this unproved general induction hypothesis for each F_c, the finite-list lemma—and hence the required finiteness mechanism—is not established as written.
